Monet's 1872 painting, source of the movement's name.
Adjacent strokes of pure colour mixed optically by the viewer.
1863 exhibition for works rejected by the official Paris Salon.

walkthroughs.body_html: In 1863, Emperor Napoleon III authorised the Salon des Refusés to exhibit works rejected by the official Salon. Manet's Déjeuner sur l'herbe caused scandal; modern art's break with academic painting began.

The first Impressionist exhibition opened in April 1874 in Nadar's studio. Monet's Impression, Sunrise (1872), painted at Le Havre, gave critic Louis Leroy the dismissive title that became the movement's name.
Industrial paint in tubes (introduced from the 1840s) enabled plein-air work. Impressionists used short strokes of unmixed colour, allowing the eye to fuse them — anticipating Pointillism.
